title: Origo Cantuum Et Cursum Ecclesiasticorum Ex Codice Vetustissimo
author: Anonymous
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1230.tmp1230.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Beatus Trosimus episcopus Arelatensis, et sanctus Photinus martyr et episcopus Lugdunensis, discipulus sancti Petri apostoli, sicut et refert Josephus et Eusebius Cæsariensis episcopus, cursum Romanum in Galleis tradiderunt.
passages.english: Blessed Trophimus, bishop of Arles, and Saint Photinus, martyr and bishop of Lyon, a disciple of Saint Peter the apostle, as both Josephus and Eusebius bishop of Caesarea report, handed down the Roman office (cursus) in the Gauls.
passages.notes: "Trosimus" is taken as Trophimus of Arles. "Photinus" is presumably Pothinus of Lyon. The attribution to Josephus is the author's own and is historically impossible.

passages.original: Inde postea relatione beati Photini martyris, cum quadraginta et octo martyribus, retrusi ergastulum, relatione ad beatum Clementem IV loci successuris Petri apostoli deportaverunt, et beatum Inerenium episcopum beatus Clemens ordinavit, Hoc in libro sancti ipsius Inerenii episcopi et martyris reperies. EJoctus a beato Polycarno Hismerniorum episcopum et martyrem, qui fuit discipulus Johannis apostoli, sicut refert historiograffus Josephus et Hiereneus episcopi in suo libro.
passages.english: Afterwards, from there, by the report of blessed Photinus the martyr, [who] with forty-eight martyrs [had been] thrust into prison, they carried a report to blessed Clement, the fourth in place of succession to Peter the apostle, and blessed Clement ordained blessed Irenaeus as bishop. You will find this in the book of the same Saint Irenaeus, bishop and martyr. [He was] taught by blessed Polycarp, bishop and martyr of the Smyrnaeans, who was a disciple of John the apostle, as the historian Josephus and bishop Irenaeus report in his book.
passages.notes: The Latin is very ungrammatical and probably corrupt, so the construction is uncertain. "retrusi ergastulum" is read as "thrust into prison". "successuris" is read as "successionis". "EJoctus" is read as "Doctus" (taught). "Inerenium", "Inerenii" and "Hiereneus" are all taken as Irenaeus. "Polycarno Hismerniorum" is taken as Polycarp of the Smyrnaeans.

passages.original: Sed beatus Marcus evangelista, sicut refert Josephus et Eusebius in libro iv, totam Ægyptum vel Italiam taliier praedicaverunt, sicut unam Ecclesiam, ut omnis sanctus, vel Gloria in excelsis Deo, vel oratione Dominica, et Amen universi tam viri quam feminx decantarent.
passages.english: But blessed Mark the evangelist, as Josephus and Eusebius report in book 4, preached throughout all Egypt and Italy in such a way, as a single Church, that all, both men and women, would sing together the Sanctus, the Gloria in excelsis Deo, the Lord's Prayer and the Amen.
passages.notes: "taliier" is read as "taliter" and "feminx" as "feminae". "omnis sanctus" is taken as the Sanctus ("the Holy, holy"). The plural verb "praedicaverunt" with a singular subject is the original's own grammar.

passages.original: Beatus Hieronymus adfirmaL ipsum cursum qui dicitur præsente tempore Scottorum, beatus Marcus decantavit, et post ipsum Gregorius Nanzenzenus, quem Hieronymus suum magistrum esse adfirmat. Et beatus Basilius frater ipsius sancti Gregorii, Antonius, Paulus, Macharius, vel Johannes et Malchus secundum ordinem Patrum decantaverunt.
passages.english: Blessed Jerome affirms that blessed Mark sang the very office (cursus) which at the present time is called that of the Scots [i.e. the Irish], and after him Gregory of Nazianzus, whom Jerome affirms to have been his teacher. And blessed Basil, brother of that same Saint Gregory, [and] Antony, Paul, Macarius, John and Malchus sang it according to the order of the Fathers.
passages.notes: "adfirmaL" is read as "adfirmat". The author calls Basil Gregory's brother, though Basil's brother was Gregory of Nyssa, not Gregory of Nazianzus.

passages.original: Est et alius cursus quem refert beatus Augustinus episcopus, quod beatus Ambrosius propter hæreticorum ordinem dissimilem composuit, quem in Italia antea decantabatur.
passages.english: There is also another office (cursus), which blessed Augustine the bishop reports, which blessed Ambrose composed on account of the heretics, different in arrangement, which was formerly sung in Italy.
passages.notes: "propter hæreticorum ordinem dissimilem" is awkward. It may mean "different from the order of the heretics" or "on account of the heretics, with a different order".
